-116.18800,43.60320.name: Idaho Center for Reproductive Medicine
-116.18800,43.60320.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Cristin C. Slater, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

121.00434,31.38194.name: CTI Biotechnology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd.
121.00434,31.38194.state: KUNSHAN, SUZHOU CITY, JIANGSU PROVINCE, P.R. CHINA
121.00434,31.38194.company: Centre Testing International Group Co., Ltd. (CTI)
121.00434,31.38194.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Centre Testing International Group Co., Ltd. (CTI). Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.49475,53.37906.name: Jessop Fertility
-1.49475,53.37906.state: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Jessop Wing, Tree Root Walk, Sheffield, S10 2SF, United Kingdom
-1.49475,53.37906.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-122.93188,49.25519.name: Amgen British Columbia
-122.93188,49.25519.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, December 2023
-122.93188,49.25519.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, December 2023. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-74.05069,4.66183.name: Instituto de Fertilidad Humana - In Ser Bogota
-74.05069,4.66183.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.inser.com.co. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-77.42313,39.43818.name: U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID)
-77.42313,39.43818.state: 1425 Porter St, Frederick, MD 21702, United States, United States
-77.42313,39.43818.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by U.S. Army. It is categorised as a defense laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

73.04790,33.68440.name: National Biosafety Centre (Pakistan) — Ministry of Climate Change
73.04790,33.68440.desc: Pakistan’s biosafety body, in a country where Bt cotton spread widely before any formal approval process was functioning. The seed moved through informal channels ahead of the regulator, which is the sequence several countries have followed and which no register captures.

8.54000,47.37600.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
8.54000,47.37600.desc: Co-developed Casgevy with Vertex, the first CRISPR therapy approved anywhere, cleared in the UK and US in late 2023 for sickle cell disease and beta thalassaemia. The company was co-founded by Emmanuelle Charpentier, so a share of the foundational patents and the first approved product sit in the same lineage. The treatment works: it edits a patient's own blood stem cells outside the body and returns them. It also costs over two million dollars per patient and requires a transplant-capable hospital, which means the disease it cures most often occurs in places that cannot deliver it — the sharpest example on this map of a technology working and reaching almost nobody.

-70.65000,-33.44000.name: ANASAC / Chilean seed multiplication
-70.65000,-33.44000.desc: Counter-season seed multiplication for northern hemisphere breeders, which is a large and little-discussed part of the world seed system. Chile grows engineered seed for export that its own farmers may not plant, so the country carries the agronomic risk of a crop it has not approved for itself.

-71.14200,42.39000.name: Synlogic
-71.14200,42.39000.desc: Engineered bacteria taken as medicine, designed to break down compounds the patient cannot metabolise and built to die outside the gut. It wound down its lead programme in 2024 after trial results, which is worth recording: a living engineered medicine that reached patients and then did not work is part of the history of this field.

4.85700,45.78200.name: Interpol — bioterrorism prevention programme
4.85700,45.78200.desc: Trains police and customs services on detecting the misuse of biological material and coordinates investigations across borders. It is the only body in this field whose work can end in an arrest rather than a guideline. The Global BioLabs assessment places it among the international organisations that have the resources to act and put biorisk management low on their own list of priorities, which is that report's recurring finding about every large institution in this space.
